Fields: candidates (title, first_published, one_line, who) and items (one row per cited URL: slug, role source or reaction, i the index, kind, url or null, title, claim).

candidates.title: Four superheavy elements are recognised, completing the periodic table's seventh row
who: RIKEN Nishina Center, Japan (Kosuke Morita group, element 113)
Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna, with Lawrence Livermore and Oak Ridge National Laboratories (elements 115, 117 and 118)
candidates.one_line: An IUPAC and IUPAP expert panel recognised the discovery of elements 113, 115, 117 and 118, the last four of the seventh row. A team at GSI in Germany had reproduced element 117 in 2014.

candidates.title: Borophene, a one-atom-thick metal sheet of pure boron, is made and confirmed
who: Northwestern University and Argonne National Laboratory (Mark Hersam and Nathan Guisinger groups)
candidates.one_line: Northwestern and Argonne researchers grew atomically thin boron sheets on silver, as theory had predicted, and showed they conduct like a metal. A Chinese team reported similar sheets in March 2016.

candidates.title: Independent labs find LK-99 is not a room-temperature superconductor
who: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart (Pascal Puphal, Bernhard Keimer)
Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing (Shilin Zhu, Jianlin Luo; from memory)
University of Manchester (Ivan Timokhin, Artem Mishchenko; from memory)
candidates.one_line: Within weeks, labs in Germany, China, the UK and the US found that LK-99 does not superconduct, and that copper sulfide in the samples explains the claimed signs.

candidates.title: A strict test shows most electric ammonia claims lacked proof, except lithium-mediated
who: Technical University of Denmark (Ib Chorkendorff and Jens Nørskov groups)
Stanford University (Thomas Jaramillo, Stacey Bent and Matteo Cargnello groups; from memory)
Imperial College London (Ifan Stephens; from memory)
candidates.one_line: A team from Denmark, the US and the UK showed how to check electric ammonia from nitrogen with isotope labels. It found no ammonia from the best aqueous metal catalysts, and proved ammonia from a lithium route.

candidates.title: Two teams use neural networks to solve the Schrödinger equation for molecules
ai_systems: FermiNet (Fermionic Neural Network), Google DeepMind and Imperial College London
who: Google DeepMind with Imperial College London (David Pfau, James Spencer, Alexander Matthews, Matthew Foulkes)
candidates.one_line: DeepMind and Imperial researchers trained a neural network to represent the electrons of a small molecule and solve its quantum equation without training data. A Berlin team independently built a similar network, PauliNet.

candidates.title: Ebola vaccine protects in Guinea ring trial, then wins approval
candidates.one_line: In a 2015 ring vaccination trial in Guinea, the rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine prevented Ebola in contacts of cases. The vaccine, later called Ervebo, was approved by the US FDA and the European Union in late 2019.

candidates.title: First KRAS-targeting cancer drug, sotorasib, wins FDA approval for lung cancer
who: University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
candidates.one_line: Sotorasib blocks a mutant form of KRAS, a cancer driver long judged undruggable. After early trials, the FDA gave it accelerated approval in May 2021 for lung cancer with the KRAS G12C change.

candidates.title: Prime editing rewrites DNA without cutting both strands or using donor DNA
who: Liu lab, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
candidates.one_line: Prime editing is a CRISPR-based tool that copies a short typed-in DNA sequence into a chosen spot, without cutting both DNA strands or supplying a separate donor DNA piece. Other labs have used it in plants and other organisms.

candidates.title: Two brain implants turn attempted speech into text and voice
ai_systems: Deep learning speech and avatar decoder (UCSF)
candidates.one_line: Two teams, at Stanford and UCSF, reported brain implants that let people who cannot speak, one with ALS and one after a stroke, communicate faster than earlier devices by decoding attempted speech with neural networks.

candidates.title: R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine protects children and gains WHO prequalification
who: Clinical Research Unit of Nanoro, Burkina Faso
candidates.one_line: In Burkina Faso, a low-dose R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine given to young children before the rainy season cut clinical malaria in a randomised trial. WHO recommended it in October 2023 and prequalified it in December 2023.

candidates.title: NOAA puts three AI global weather models into daily operation
candidates.one_line: On 17 December 2025 NOAA put three AI-driven global weather models into operation at the National Weather Service: AIGFS, AIGEFS and the hybrid HGEFS, which combines AI and physics-based ensemble forecasts.

candidates.title: Google DeepMind's cyclone model is used by the US National Hurricane Center
who: US National Hurricane Center (NOAA National Weather Service)
candidates.one_line: In 2025 Google DeepMind put an experimental AI cyclone model online in its Weather Lab, and the US National Hurricane Center used it as one of its forecast guidance tools during the hurricane season.

candidates.title: Mass bleaching hits the Great Barrier Reef in 2016
who: James Cook University and the ARC Centre of Excellence for Coral Reef Studies (Hughes et al.)
candidates.one_line: In 2016 mass coral bleaching struck the Great Barrier Reef for the third time since 1998. Aerial surveys of thousands of reefs found the worst damage in the north; the Nature study links it to rising sea temperatures.

candidates.title: A Mars rover uses AI software to choose its own laser targets
candidates.one_line: Since 2016 NASA's Curiosity rover has used AEGIS, software that NASA calls AI, to choose rock targets and aim its ChemCam laser on its own, without waiting for instructions from Earth.

candidates.title: Large project retests social-science claims and about half replicate
candidates.one_line: A collaboration of 865 researchers retested claims from social and behavioural science papers for replicability, reproducibility and robustness. Three Nature papers report that roughly half of the retested claims held up.

candidates.title: Short chats with AI chatbots shift voters' political preferences
ai_systems: GPT-4o (OpenAI), to be checked against the two papers
who: Cornell University and MIT (Lin et al., Nature)
University of Oxford and London School of Economics (Hackenburg et al., Science)
candidates.one_line: Two papers published together tested AI chatbots that talk with voters. Short conversations moved people's stated preferences, and the most persuasive set-ups packed in more factual claims, which were less accurate on average.

candidates.title: ChatGPT labels text for social science better than crowd workers
candidates.one_line: In five labelling tasks on tweets and news, ChatGPT's zero-shot accuracy beat crowd workers on four and its agreement was higher on all, at about twenty times lower cost. Other teams later reproduced the pattern with GPT-4.

candidates.title: Phone data and machine learning pick who gets emergency cash in Togo
ai_systems: machine-learning model trained on mobile phone records and surveys (UC Berkeley and Northwestern University researchers)
candidates.one_line: In 2020 Togo's government paid emergency cash to people chosen with a model trained on mobile phone records. A Nature study found it targeted poorer people better than geography-based methods, while missing some of the poor.

candidates.title: Chats with an AI chatbot weaken belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.one_line: About 2,000 US adults who believed a conspiracy theory had a short chat with a GPT-4 Turbo chatbot that offered tailored facts. Belief fell by about a fifth on average, and the drop lasted at least two months.

candidates.title: AI assistant raises customer-support productivity in a large field study
ai_systems: GPT-based conversational assistant (OpenAI model family), deployed by a software firm
candidates.one_line: In a field study of about 5,000 customer-support agents, access to a generative AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by about 14 percent, with the largest gains for the least experienced workers.

candidates.title: Replication of 21 social-science experiments from Nature and Science
who: Social Sciences Replication Project (Camerer, Dreber, Johannesson and others)
candidates.one_line: A team repeated 21 social-science experiments first published in Nature and Science from 2010 to 2015, with much larger samples. Thirteen replicated, and the repeat effects were on average about half the size of the originals.

candidates.title: Six trials in six countries find microcredit gains modest
who: Six independent research teams, one for each country
Innovations for Poverty Action and the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (partners in several trials)
candidates.one_line: Six randomised trials of microcredit in six countries, published together, found modest gains in business activity but no clear gain in average household income or wellbeing.

candidates.title: National experiment finds a short growth-mindset lesson helps some students
who: National Study of Learning Mindsets team
candidates.one_line: A national randomised study of over 12,000 US ninth-graders found a short online growth-mindset lesson raised lower achievers' grades and advanced maths enrolment, with effects clustered in schools with supportive peer norms.

candidates.title: Global online game maps moral preferences for self-driving car dilemmas
candidates.one_line: An online game collected about 40 million decisions from people in 233 countries and territories on whom a self-driving car should spare, finding shared preferences and three regional clusters.

candidates.title: An entire carbonised Herculaneum scroll is read for the first time
ai_systems: Machine-learning ink-detection and virtual-unwrapping software of the Vesuvius Challenge and the Digital Restoration Initiative, University of Kentucky (exact names and makers not read)
who: Digital Restoration Initiative, University of Kentucky
Diamond Light Source (UK) and ESRF (France), scanning partners (roles not read)
candidates.one_line: Researchers virtually unwrapped an entire rolled Herculaneum papyrus from X-ray scans and, with AI help, read its complete text: the first whole carbonised scroll read without opening it.

candidates.title: Ancient DNA links Minoans and Mycenaeans to early Aegean farmers
who: Iosif Lazaridis, David Reich and colleagues, Harvard Medical School (memory)
candidates.one_line: Genomes of ancient people from Crete, mainland Greece and Anatolia showed Minoans and Mycenaeans were closely related, both descended mostly from early Aegean farmers with some Caucasus or Iran-related ancestry, and Mycenaeans also had steppe-related ancestry.

candidates.title: First whole genome from ancient Egypt, from a 4,800-year-old man
who: Liverpool John Moores University (Linus Girdland-Flink) and the Francis Crick Institute (Pontus Skoglund), with co-authors (memory)
candidates.one_line: DNA from the teeth of a man buried at Nuwayrat in the Old Kingdom gave the first whole genome from ancient Egypt: about four-fifths North African ancestry and about one-fifth from the eastern Fertile Crescent.

candidates.title: One AI model translates between 200 languages, many with little text
who: UC Berkeley and Johns Hopkins University co-authors (memory)
candidates.one_line: Meta's NLLB-200 model translates directly between 200 languages, including many with little written text, and scored better than earlier systems on average in tests against human-checked benchmarks.

candidates.title: Earliest known wooden structure, built at least 476,000 years ago in Zambia
who: University of Liverpool (Larry Barham) and Aberystwyth University (Geoff Duller), with co-authors (memory)
candidates.one_line: Luminescence dating of cut, interlocking logs preserved in waterlogged deposits at Kalambo Falls, Zambia, gave a minimum age of 476,000 years, showing early hominins shaped wood into a structure long before Homo sapiens.

candidates.title: Oldest known story-telling cave art found in Sulawesi, 51,200 years old
who: Griffith University (Maxime Aubert, Adam Brumm) and BRIN, Indonesia (Adhi Agus Oktaviana), with co-authors (memory)
candidates.one_line: A cave painting in Sulawesi, Indonesia, of human-like figures with a pig was dated, through uranium-series dating of mineral crusts over it, to at least 51,200 years ago: the oldest known narrative art.
